To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the adherence of bovine polymorhphonuclear cells to glass and plastic is active, independent of divalent ions and inhibited by metabolic inhibitors.

the PMN adherence to naked plastic, glass, or nylon wool fibers is active and resistant to the action of metabolic inhibitors, whereas cell spreading on these surfaces is sensitive to metabolic inhibition.
PMN adhere strongly and flatten on naked surfaces, and that this process requires an intact glycolysis and oxidative metabolism, but is independent of divalent ions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the environment on the locomotory activity of bovine PMN.
the effect of proteins and inhibitors on the adhesion and spreading of bovine PMN on plastic, glass or nylon fibers and on the migration of bovine PM under agarose.
the effect of proteins and inhibitors on cell adherence and spreading and on the chemotactic response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

PMN adherence is an active process, independent of divalent ions, which occurs in the absence of protein, but which is strongly inhibited by some proteins, and that the presence of protein in the medium is a prerequisite for chemotaxis.

PMN adherence and spreading are active and independent of divalent ions, but that cell-surface interactions are reduced by some of the proteins tested, and that this effect may be related to the ability of PMN to respond to chemoattractant gradients.

the PMN adherence and spreading on surfaces is a complex process, which involves a number of different metabolic events, including glycolysis, oxidative metabolism, and the presence of serum proteins, which may act either by reducing the cell-surface interactions or by increasing the cell-matrix interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

PMN adherence is a process that is independent of glycolysis and oxidative phosphorylation, but requires a temperature of 37 degrees C, whereas cell spreading requires an intact glycolysis and an intact oxidative pathway.

the proteins tested in the present work affected the PMN adherence by modifying the cell-surface properties and that this effect was not necessarily correlated with the ability of the proteins to act as serum chemoattractive factors.
the adherence of bovine PMN to plastic is an active process that is not mediated by divalent cations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PMN adherence to naked plastic is an active and energy-dependent process that is inhibited by metabolic inhibitors.
the presence of proteins in the medium is required for PMN to respond well to chemoattractant gradients.
proteins can be used to control cell-surface interactions, and that these interactions can be modulated by metabolic inhibitors.
